I've been farming these 18 mu for a long time, and wheat after maize is what everyone around here does. I'll keep doing what worked last year because changing things is risky.

For the winter wheat, I'll plant in early October after the maize comes off. I use improved seed from the agricultural supply shop — the shop owner sells what most of us buy, yield is steady around 450-480 kg per mu if the weather is decent. Before planting I'll spread diammonium phosphate as base fertilizer, about 40 kg per mu (that's one bag for every mu and a bit), which gives me around 7 kg phosphorus and 7 kg nitrogen on the ground from the start. Then at jointing in March I top-dress with urea, about 25 kg per mu — that's the critical time, I don't skimp because a weak wheat crop means losing hundreds of yuan per mu. I also add potassium chloride, maybe 8 kg per mu at base, since my neighbor said the soil has gotten tired. Total nitrogen comes to around 18-19 kg per mu.

Wheat irrigation: I have the well, so I water at overwintering, jointing, and heading — three times usually, sometimes four if spring is dry. Pesticide: one herbicide in spring, one for aphids and powdery mildew around flowering, and sometimes a second spray if I see rust. Call it 2-3 times. I rotary-till before planting, nobody around here does plough anymore — too slow and too expensive.

For the summer maize after wheat harvest in June, I direct-seed with no-till using a hybrid seed (Zhengdan or similar, whatever the shop recommends that year). At sowing I put down compound fertilizer, about 40 kg per mu. Then at the big trumpet stage I side-dress urea, 20 kg per mu. Maize is hungrier than wheat, I don't cut back here. One or two waterings if July-August is dry. Pesticide mainly for corn borer, one or two sprays. I expect about 550-600 kg per mu, that's what I've been getting.

I spend more on fertilizer than some experts say I need to, but I'd rather lose a few hundred yuan on extra urea than lose a thousand yuan on a thin crop. That's the calculation for me.
